citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Passarowitz put Oltenia under Habsburg administration for twenty-one years; the principality east of the Olt is the phase drawn here.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Belgrade returned Oltenia. The phase runs to the double election of 1859, where this layer stops.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Twenty-one years of Habsburg administration west of the Olt, and the reason this layer models phases rather than one timeless Wallachia.

instrument: Consolidation of Ottoman suzerainty after Mohács
citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Carpathians to the Dniester. Cetatea Albă and the Budjak had already been detached to direct Ottoman administration and are not separated here, which is a known simplification.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: The north-western districts, with the old capital at Suceava, pass to the Habsburgs.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: The Prut becomes the eastern boundary. The phase runs to 1859.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Detached from Moldavia and administered from Vienna; a duchy in its own right from 1849.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Between the Prut and the Dniester. The southern districts returned to Moldavia in 1856 and are not drawn as a separate phase; that omission is recorded as verification debt.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Between Ferdinand of Habsburg and János Szapolyai. The Partium, held with Transylvania in this period, is not drawn; the ring is the Carpathian core only.

instrument: Fall of Buda and the partition of Hungary
citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: The principality of the Diet and the three nations. Same ring as the phases either side of it: what changes across 1541 and 1699 is who holds it, not where the mountains are.

citation: Hertslet, The Map of Europe by Treaty, vol. I (1875)
notes: Karlowitz confirms Habsburg possession; a Grand Principality from 1765. This is the state the Josephinian survey maps.
